record.paper_title: Fair Division under Joint Ownership: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Manna division with fairness and monotonicity constraints
record.original_question: In the manna-division problem, where a fixed stock of unproduced goods is divided among agents with arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences, does there exist a Pareto optimal mechanism that satisfies Population Monotonicity and No Domination, where Population Monotonicity means that when an additional agent joins the population sharing the same cake no pre-existing agent benefits, and No Domination means that no agent ever receives a strictly bigger share of every good than another agent? If such a mechanism exists, can one also require Equal Split Guarantee, meaning that each agent's welfare is at least as high as the welfare of that agent's per-capita share of the resources?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Manna Division. Say that a mechanism satisfies No Domination (Moulin and Thomson 1988) if it never gives to an agent a strictly bigger share of all goods than to another agent. Is there a Pareto optimal mechanism satisfying Population Monotonicity and No Domination? If the answer is yes, can we also meet Equal Split Guarantee (on top of the three first properties)?
Repeated applications of inequality (5) gives the following interpretation of the axiom: an agent never benefits when the population sharing a given cake increases.
Definition 1 (Steinhaus 1948). A mechanism satisfies Equal Split Guarantee if the welfare of any agent, at any profile, is not below that of his per capita share of the resources.
In both questions we assume arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the manna-division problem: a fixed bundle of perfectly divisible, unproduced goods (a "cake") is to be divided among a finite set of agents. Each agent has an arbitrary preference relation over their share that is convex and monotonic (more of every good is weakly better, and preferences have convex upper-contour sets). A mechanism associates to every population (finite set of agents) and every profile of such preferences an allocation of the entire cake among the agents.

Define the following properties of a mechanism:

1. Pareto Optimality: at every profile, the allocation chosen is not Pareto-dominated by any other feasible allocation of the cake.

2. Population Monotonicity: if a new agent joins the population sharing the same cake (so the cake is now split among more agents), then no pre-existing agent strictly prefers the new allocation to the old one — equivalently, every pre-existing agent weakly loses.

3. No Domination: at every profile, the chosen allocation never assigns to any agent a bundle that is strictly larger in every coordinate (every good) than the bundle assigned to some other agent.

4. Equal Split Guarantee: at every profile, every agent weakly prefers their assigned bundle to receiving the equal-split bundle (the per-capita share 1/n of the cake, where n is the number of agents).

Question (a): Does there exist a mechanism on this domain (arbitrary convex monotonic preferences over a divisible heterogeneous manna) that simultaneously satisfies Pareto Optimality, Population Monotonicity, and No Domination?

Question (b): If such a mechanism exists, can one in addition require it to satisfy Equal Split Guarantee?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this combined axiomatic question for manna division with arbitrary convex monotonic preferences. Related literature (e.g., the competitive/Nash rule for mixed manna by Bogomolnaia–Moulin–Sandomirskiy–Yanovskaya, and work on population/resource monotonicity in cake-cutting) establishes monotonicity properties of specific Pareto-optimal rules in restricted domains, but does not appear to settle the existence of a Pareto-optimal mechanism satisfying both Population Monotonicity and No Domination (and additionally Equal Split Guarantee) on the general convex monotonic domain. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Competitive division of a mixed manna
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the competitive (Nash-optimal) rule for mixed manna; addresses Pareto optimality and fairness/monotonicity properties of specific rules but does not resolve the joint existence question with No Domination on the general convex-monotonic domain.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on competitive division of manna does not appear to resolve the combined axiomatic question.

status_evidence.title: Resource-monotonicity and population-monotonicity in connected cake-cutting
status_evidence.snippet: Examines monotonicity in cake-cutting; impossibility results for proportional Pareto-optimal rules motivate the search for weaker fairness notions but the precise question with No Domination remains unresolved in the surveyed literature.
status_evidence.claim: No published resolution to the existence question with Pareto Optimality + Population Monotonicity + No Domination was located.
